title: Recognizing and avoiding redundant ORM queries

steps.title: Recognizing and avoiding redundant ORM queries

blocks.text: Lazy relationship access can emit extra SELECTs. Loading a relationship separately for each parent can produce N+1 queries.
Use statement.options(selectinload(Entity.relationship_attribute)) to fetch the selected parents’ collection with an additional batched query, not one per parent.
joinedload(...) instead uses a join. For collection loading, apply Result.unique() as required to deduplicate parents.
Compare emitted SQL before and after with engine echo=True; confirm fewer relationship queries and unchanged returned entity data.

from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey, create_engine, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship, Session, selectinload
class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass
class Entity(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'Entity'
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    relationship_attribute: Mapped[list['Child']] = relationship(back_populates='parent')
class Child(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'relationship_attribute'
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    parent_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey('Entity.id'))
    parent: Mapped[Entity] = relationship(back_populates='relationship_attribute')
engine = create_engine('sqlite://', echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
with Session(engine) as session:
    session.add_all([Entity(id=11),Entity(id=22),Entity(id=33),
                     Child(id=111,parent_id=11),Child(id=112,parent_id=11),Child(id=221,parent_id=22)])
    session.commit()
def listing(session):
    statement = select(Entity).order_by(Entity.id).limit(3)
    statement = statement.options(selectinload(Entity.relationship_attribute))
    parents = session.execute(statement).scalars().all()
    return [{'id':p.id, 'children':[c.id for c in p.relationship_attribute]} for p in parents]
# Run baseline and changed listing in separate fresh sessions and capture echo
# output; do not reuse already-loaded relationships when measuring the change.
if __name__ == '__main__':
    with Session(engine) as session:
        print(listing(session))

steps.title: Recognizing and avoiding redundant ORM queries

segments.label: Replace per-movie review queries with selectinload
segments.summary: Accessing a movie's reviews can issue a separate SELECT because the relationship is loaded lazily. Listing eight movies and accessing each collection produces nine queries: one for the movies and eight for their reviews. With engine echo logging enabled, the demonstration exposes these repeated queries, then imports selectinload from sqlalchemy.orm and adds options(selectinload(Movie.reviews)) to the statement. The resulting SQL retrieves the movies first, then fetches their reviews together using the selected movie IDs in an IN clause. For this listing, the query count falls from nine to two without introducing a join. The demonstration uses synchronous session execution.

blocks.group_title: Recognize N+1 queries and batch collection loading

bridge.before: Watch for relationship SELECTs and the selectinload option. The clip uses synchronous execution; with AsyncSession, await execution and do not assume implicit lazy I/O works the same way.
bridge.after: The clip shows nine queries becoming two. The text also covers joinedload with Result.unique() and explicitly checking unchanged returned entity data, which the clip does not fully verify.

Add selectinload(Entity.relationship_attribute) through statement.options(...) to fetch a collection relationship for the selected parents with an additional batched query rather than one query per parent.
